The 6 DAG-only nodes are architecturally interesting

Those deserve a note because they indicate one of two things:

Planned semantic concepts that never became columns.
Historical columns that disappeared but left DAG residue.

Neither of those two is what these six are. None of them is a column that used to sit on enriched_df and was deleted. feature_pipeline.py never assigns any of the six names. Git history of that file has no total_wick, no displacement_retrace, no displacement_atr_ratio, and no disp_strength_atr_rescale. ema_spread_atr and momentum_score_atr appear once, in a docstring that says the column names stay ema_spread and momentum_score.

The DAG comment that introduces four of them already says they are not in the vector. That comment still says "39-vector". The vector is 48. The exclusion is still true.

They are on the DAG because feature_dag_layers.py merges ontology identities, and these six are registered identities with an empty vector_key. Empty vector_key means "not a canonical slot", not "a slot we lost".

total_wick, FM-005. Registered candle primitive, upper_wick + lower_wick. The frame writes upper_wick and lower_wick in compute_price_features and does not write the sum. The scalar exists in candle_math.total_wick. live_engine_hook uses it as a local wick_size, not as a frame column. This is the closest of the six to a concept that never became a column. It was not a column that disappeared.

ema_spread_atr, FM-030, and momentum_score_atr, FM-031. A second formula for columns that already exist. lifecycle parity_verified, active false. The active config sets normalization_basis to atr_relative, so this run writes FM-022 into ema_spread and FM-023 into momentum_score. The atr_absolute arm would write FM-030 and FM-031 into those same two columns. The ontology says they add no slot. The old migration_candidates block is still in the yaml, marked as the 2026-07-12 proposal, and it is not the authority. Not a missing column. Not a deleted column.

displacement_retrace, FM-027, and displacement_atr_ratio, FM-028. These are emitted. The object is the CRT episode cache, state.cached_features, built inside try_expansion_to_retest. lineage.scope is EPISODE. vector_key is empty on purpose. The ontology says the pipeline has no displacement-candle / retest-candle pair, so adding a frame column would not be this identity. The historical part is a rename on that cache, not a dropped frame column: the same numbers used to be stored under retest_depth and disp_strength, which collided with FM-021 and FM-020. CH-002 gave the cache its own keys. crt_engine_v2 still aliases them back to the old names only at the BitNet input boundary.

disp_strength_atr_rescale, FM-029. A third local quantity inside scoring_engine.compute_scores. The ontology says it was registered to separate that local from FM-020 and FM-028, not because the quantity is wanted. Produced and consumed by scoring_engine. vector_key empty. This is residue of a local score input. It is not residue of a frame column.

So the DAG is wider than the frame on purpose. Four of the six are live math on other objects. One is a scalar that was never stored. Two are an inactive formula for columns the frame already has.

Now look for costmodel schema and producers and consumers

There is no single cost-model schema. Four objects use that name, and their ids do not join by string equality. `docs/governance/schema_version_registry.json` does not register any of them. Active config is `v2_htfcrt_2026_08`. No source or config edit.

The one that decomposes broker cost is SEM-015, `ComponentCostModel` in `src/research/costs.py`.

Fields, price units per unit traded, not basis points:

| Field | Role |
|---|---|
| half_spread | crossed on entry and on exit |
| commission | per leg, stored as a magnitude |
| entry_slippage | market-order drift on entry |
| stop_slippage | added only when `exit_kind` is `SL_HIT` |
| swap_long_per_night | signed; None means unmeasured |
| swap_short_per_night | same |
| instrument, source, status | provenance; status is MEASURED, INSUFFICIENT_DATA, or UNKNOWN |
| entry_slippage_basis | MEASURED or PROXY_FROM_STOP |

Charge, from `cost_price`: entry leg is half_spread + commission + entry_slippage. Exit leg is half_spread + commission, plus stop_slippage only for `SL_HIT`. A take-profit and a timeout do not pay stop slippage. Overnight carry is added only when `nights_held > 0` and the swap is a debit. A credit is not subtracted. `cost_r` is that price divided by `risk_distance`. The `entry` argument is accepted and unused. Only status MEASURED may charge. An unmeasured component is a raise, not a silent zero.

The XAUUSD factory `xau_measured_cost_model()` hardcodes half_spread 0.045, commission 0.040, entry_slippage 0.090, stop_slippage 0.090, both swaps None, basis PROXY_FROM_STOP. It does not read the calibration file. `from_manifest` does, and it will load swap from the manifest or from `outputs.swap_json` when that file says MEASURED.

Producers of the measured numbers:

- `src/research/mt5_cost_calibration.py` `compute_c_per_side` writes `c_per_side.components`: half_spread_usd, commission_per_oz_usd, stop_slippage_usd. It does not emit entry_slippage. Status is the worst of spread, commission, and stop slippage.
- `scripts/research/xauusd_mt5_cost_calibration.py` writes the manifest: title, generated_utc, symbol, windows, statuses, c_per_side, outputs (spread csv, commission json, slippage csv, swap json, plus sha256 of each).

Producers of the object:

- `ComponentCostModel.from_manifest` — `src/research/runner.py` `_bind_cost_model`, `src/research/visual_crt/measure.py`, `src/research/oracle/labeler.py`, `src/research/probes/costs_path.py`, `scripts/research/exit_geometry_scan.py`, and the three `scripts/analysis/phase1_*` census scripts.
- `xau_measured_cost_model()` — `src/research/mother_range/driver.py`, `src/research/sujan_crt/driver.py`, `scripts/research/ultron_sem_r_shadow.py`. These never see a later change to the manifest.

Consumers of the charge (`cost_r`, `net_rr`, or `cost_price`):

- `src/research/measurement/metrics.py` `EdgeAggregator.aggregate`. The signature says `CostModel`, but if `net_rr` accepts `exit_kind` it passes the outcome. That is how the runner's component model reaches a net R.
- `src/research/oracle/labeler.py`, `oracle/exit_sweep.py`, `oracle/exit_analysis.py`.
- `src/research/visual_crt/driver.py` and `measure.py`.
- `src/research/mother_range/driver.py` and `sujan_crt/driver.py`, through `research.mc_kit.trade.exit_kind`.
- `src/research/probes/costs_path.py` and `probes/phase1_replay.py` (the replay function takes a model; it does not build one).
- `src/research/provenance.py` `truth_standard_block` does not charge. It stores `provenance()`, whose `cost_model_id` is the string `component_measured.v1`.

The ontology node SEM-015 lists producers `mt5_cost_calibration.py` and `costs.py`, and consumers `costs.py`, `metrics.py`, `provenance.py`. That list is the registration. It is not the live call list above.

The flat model is the other class in the same file. Schema is one field, `round_trip_bps`, default 12. `cost_r` is `(bps / 10000) * entry / risk_distance`. Instances are `DEFAULT_COST_MODEL` and `ZERO_COST`. `ResearchConfig.cost_model` defaults to `flat_bps` and also accepts `component_measured`, which then requires `costs.cost_model_manifest_path`. Consumers are `EdgeAggregator`, `qualification.py`, `qualify_matrix.py`, `regime_conditioning.py`, `exit_grid.py`, `forensics.py`, the two gaussian zone-mapping evals, and the `scripts/research/qualify_*.py` family. They import `CostModel`, not `ComponentCostModel`.

Production backtest is a third schema, and it does not import `research.costs`. `BacktestConfig` stamps `cost_model_id` `backtest_g1g2_v2` and a 16-hex hash of four knobs: slippage_enabled, slippage_atr_fraction, slippage_seed, simulated_spread_pct. On the active config those are true, 0.1, 42, and 0.0002. `SlippageModel` draws an adverse uniform slip in `[0, fraction * ATR]` on entry and on exit. Spread half is `close * simulated_spread_pct / 2`, applied on both sides. There is no commission field and no swap field. The stamp is written onto the trade row, the summary, and the report by `src/runtime/backtest_v2.py`. `backtest_zero_cost` is reserved and not generated.

`UltronRiskGate` is a fourth surface, not SEM-015. The active config declares `spread_pips` 0, `slippage_pips` 0, `min_sl_pips` 0. The comment on those keys says the tax is dormant at those zeros.

The closed name list in `src/identity/tokens.py` `COST_MODEL_IDS` is `flat_12bps`, `sem015_component_xauusd`, `none_gross`, `backtest_g1g2_v2`, `backtest_zero_cost`. `identity/outcome.py` and `identity/check.py` refuse any other L5 string. None of those five strings is what the other layers emit:

| Layer | String it actually writes |
|---|---|
| `ComponentCostModel.provenance()` | `component_measured.v1` |
| metals profile `metals_mt5.v1.json` | `component_measured.v1` |
| oracle labeler manifest, and the V2 measurement contracts | `CM-XAUUSD-COMPONENT-MEASURED-V1` |
| older contracts | `CM-XAUUSD-LEGACY-12BPS-UNCALIBRATED` |
| `ResearchConfig.cost_model` | `flat_bps` or `component_measured` |
| L5 vocabulary | `sem015_component_xauusd` |
| backtest stamp | `backtest_g1g2_v2` |

`visual_crt/measure.py` accepts a contract id that starts with `CM-XAUUSD-COMPONENT-MEASURED` or `CM-XAUUSD-LEGACY-12BPS`, then still builds the object from the manifest named inside the contract text. A grep of `src/` shows `sem015_component_xauusd` only in `tokens.py`. Nothing there equates it to `component_measured.v1`.
